english_translation: It follows from this knowledge that God is one, therefore no opposite can be conceived. See how those who imagine many principles, many gods, are in error. It follows immediately that God is most true. What does he who is existence itself have which might appear to be and not be? It follows certainly that he is truth itself.
exegesis: Pico contrasts God's mode of being, unity, truth, and goodness with that of all creatures, including angels. God possesses being, one, truth, and goodness identically and essentially—they are not acquired properties but the very essence of divinity. Creatures, by contrast, have these properties participated from God, received from another, and proportional to their degree in the hierarchy. This Creator-creature distinction is the metaphysical foundation for the entire angelic hierarchy. Angels are beings (not non-being), one (not divided), true (conforming to their exemplar), and good (oriented toward their source)—but all these they possess as participated properties. The seraph, as the highest creature, possesses these properties to the maximum degree possible for a creature, approaching but never equaling God's essential simplicity. This passage establishes that the hierarchy of being reaches its apex with God (essential being) and descends through angels (participated being at its highest).
metaphysical_theme: God's essential unity and being vs. creatures' participated unity and being; the Creator-creature distinction as the ontological hierarchy that positions angels as the highest participated beings

notes: HARVESTER passage U.5.1 is the apex of the metaphysical argument. It consolidates all previous distinctions into the fundamental principle: God is; creatures have being. This distinction grounds the entire hierarchy and justifies Pico's rejection of polytheism or emanationism that blurs the Creator-creature boundary. The hierarchy of being flows from this distinction: angels, as the highest creatures, most perfectly exemplify participated being, yet remain absolutely distinct from God's essential being.
